correctness.rationale: The pair (B_q,X_q) with B_q the join of q two-point sets and X_q its codimension-one skeleton gives 0→H_{q-1}(B_q)→H_{q-1}(B_q,X_q)=E→H~_{q-2}(X_q)→0. Orient facets by coordinate order; the signed fundamental cycle z=Σ_b (-1)^{|b|}e_b is primitive, and W_q acts on its line via det ε. E restricted to T=(C2)^q is a free regular lattice, hence projective, and Hom_T(E,Zε)=Z. The restriction of its generator a(e_b)=(-1)^{|b|} to z has multiplier 2^q; the Hom–Ext connecting long exact sequence therefore identifies Ext^1_T(M,Zε)=Z/2^q, with the actual extension a generator. The same a is equivariant for coordinate permutations with facet orientation sign and all flips, giving 2^q times the extension class zero over W; restriction forces order >=2^q, so its exact W order is 2^q. Dividing a by 2^q splits after inverting two. Independent finite signed-facet checks q=3,4,5 confirm face incidence cancellation and signed augmentation norm, but the all-q Hom–Ext proof supplies the quantifier.

value.rationale: The exact exponential order of an integral equivariant extension is an independently meaningful obstruction to lifting rational equivariant splittings; it pinpoints what ordinary wedge homology cannot detect and supplies a reusable signed-norm calculation on a natural hyperoctahedral family.

final_claim: For q>=3 the canonical W_q-equivariant relative-chain extension associated with the (q-2)-skeleton of the q-cross-polytope boundary has exact Yoneda Ext^1 additive order 2^q over Z[W_q], and restriction to the flip subgroup T_q generates Ext^1_Z[T_q] ≅ Z/2^q; rational/localized splitting exists but no integral splitting.
limitations: The exact Ext class concerns canonical relative-chain extension for q>=3, not ordinary homology torsion or geometric splitting.
No claim that all possible equivariant decompositions are obstructed by this particular Yoneda class.
